evidence.craft: Read src/eda_rankpayoff/rank.py (80 lines), tests/test_rank.py, experiments/run.py, build_data.py, figure.py. Stdlib only, short pure functions, common random numbers across screens (fixed seeds), figure recomputes rather than retyping, build_data asserts the two sources agree on delay and depth. Defects: inconsistent tie conventions (average ranks for Spearman, index order for top-k and best_rank) with no note; Monte Carlo (40 s, +-0.01 noise) where an exact closed form runs in 1.5 s for all 414 screens; figure.py reruns the whole measure() pass (16 s) instead of reading results; open() without close; run.py docstring says 'seconds' while README says 'about 2 minutes each' (measured 40 s and 16 s). evidence.claims: Checked against results.txt and my recomputations: headline 0.60 (0.50-0.68), -0.13 (-0.26-0.02), 0.958 -> 32%, gate count 0.551 -> 69%, 14 of 175, 204 of 207, 0.93-0.98 and 0.49-0.81 sweep ranges, named-screen values (0.931/0.936/0.937, best 5th/6th/2nd, 0.589/0.504/0.948), 0.90 (0.87-0.92) for best_rank: all backed. Limitations are unusually honest (one winner, correlated screens, optimistic bootstrap, nothing held out). Unbacked or overstated: (1) the shipped figure (experiments/figure.py:25, shown on the live page) is titled 'Rank agreement does not predict screen payoff' but plots k=3, where results.txt gives cap3 vs spearman +0.221 (0.068 to 0.360), a positive correlation whose interval excludes 0; the 'does not' finding is a k=1 result. (2) 'reproduced by independent code' (README.md:26) for 0.636/0.970/1.078: eda-latencyhalve's capture_probability is the same algorithm with random.Random(seed) and rng.sample over the same 40 rows, so the 3-dp match shows identical draws, not an independent check; the exact value is 0.646. (3) 'This asks a new question' (README.md:3) is new within the repo's eda track only; the question is studied in the performance-predictor literature, uncited. (4) 'about 2 minutes each' stale. MIT, AI-assistance and 'preliminary, not sign-off' disclaimers present.
evidence.fitness: Could a researcher build on it? As a reproducible dataset-plus-script that shows, on 40 SKY130-mapped MAC engines, that Spearman can rank screens opposite to their top-1 capture, yes: it runs in under a minute and every number checks. As a citable result, not yet. Nearest prior work: (a) White, Zela, Ru, Liu, Hutter, 'How Powerful are Performance Predictors in Neural Architecture Search?' (NeurIPS 2021) and Ning et al., 'Evaluating Efficient Performance Estimators of Neural Architectures' (NeurIPS 2021), which evaluate cheap predictors by Kendall tau and by top-k precision / search outcome and report that they disagree; Abdelfattah et al., 'Zero-Cost Proxies for Lightweight NAS' (ICLR 2021), which reports top-10% correlation for the same reason; (b) top-weighted rank agreement in IR: Yilmaz, Aslam and Robertson's AP correlation (SIGIR 2008), Webber, Moffat and Zobel's rank-biased overlap (TOIS 2010), Vigna's weighted Kendall tau (WWW 2015). None is cited, and none of those computable top-weighted measures is tested as a predictor of payoff, which is the obvious next question. With one winning design, cap1 is near-mechanically a function of where that design and its near neighbours fall (best_rank correlates 0.90), so the latency result is close to expected; the area x latency contrast is the more informative part.
evidence.domain: Against standard practice in predictor evaluation and multi-fidelity DSE: the payoff metric (P(pool best in top k) over random sub-pools) and the screen family are sensible and correctly implemented; Spearman/Kendall tau-b are textbook-correct. Departures a senior reviewer would flag: no top-weighted agreement baselines (precision@k, NDCG, weighted tau, AP-correlation), which are the field's standard answer to 'global correlation ignores the top'; inference across 207 screens of which 200 are re-weightings of one model, treated as independent (acknowledged, but no block or named-only analysis to show the sign holds); nothing held out although the recommendation is held-out evaluation; index tie-breaking in a coarse screen inflates one named row; Monte Carlo where the exact value is a one-line hypergeometric sum. Would sign off as an internal technical note for the eda track, not for a venue as is.

verdict: A small, honest, fully reproducible study: results.txt and scatter.svg regenerate byte-identically, and every headline number survives an independent recomputation with scipy's Spearman/Kendall and an exact (noise-free) hypergeometric capture probability (area x latency 0.614 vs reported 0.598; latency -0.115 vs -0.129; 14 of 175; 204 of 207). It does not meet the bar: tests caught 1 of 4 seeded mutants (tie handling and the experiment script are untested), the shipped figure's title says agreement does not predict payoff over a k=3 panel where the correlation is +0.22 with an interval excluding 0, and the question is presented as new without the NAS performance-predictor and top-weighted rank-correlation literature that already studies it, nor any computable top-weighted measure as the alternative a loop could actually use. Index tie-breaking inflates one named row (cycles alone) but not the headline.
